vulnerability.name: Path Traversal
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities allowing access to files outside intended directory
vulnerability.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive files, configuration data, or credentials
vulnerability.mitigation: Validate file paths, use allowlists, avoid using user input in file operations

findings.title: Path Traversal
findings.explanation: No input validation is performed on the `msg.data` parameter, allowing an attacker to manipulate the path traversal vulnerability.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive data or functions
exploitation_steps: Manipulate msg.data to traverse parent directories
findings.remediation: Add input validation and sanitization for the `msg.data` parameter
findings.secure_code_example: bytes4 sig = bytes4(sha3("initWallet(address[],uint256,uint256)")); address target = _walletLibrary; ... codecopy(0x0, sub(codesize, argsize), argsize); delegatecall(sub(gas, 10000), target, 0x0, add(argsize, 0x4), 0x0, 0x0)

findings.title: Path Traversal
findings.explanation: Using msg.sender.call without parameter validation allows an attacker to manipulate the function call and access files outside the intended directory.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive files, configuration data, or credentials
exploitation_steps: Send a large value for _weiToWithdraw to overflow the allowed limit
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker has control over the _weiToWithdraw variable
findings.remediation: Use parameter validation and sanitization, such as msg.sender.call.value(_weiToWithdraw, {gas: 20000})

findings.title: Path Traversal
findings.vulnerable_code: function CashOut(uint _am) public payable { if(_am<=balances[msg.sender]) { balances[msg.sender]-=_am; } }
findings.explanation: The `_am` parameter is not properly sanitized, allowing an attacker to traverse parent directories and potentially access sensitive files.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to configuration data or credentials.
exploitation_steps: Obtain the parent directory of the intended file
findings.exploitation_conditions: The contract's balance mapping is not properly validated.
findings.remediation: Sanitize user input with `require(_am < balances[msg.sender])` and validate its format.
findings.secure_code_example: function CashOut(uint _am) public payable { require(_am < balances[msg.sender]); balances[msg.sender]-=_am; }

findings.title: Path Traversal
findings.explanation: Uses msg.sender to call value(), potentially allowing a user to read files outside the intended directory.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive files or configuration data
exploitation_steps: User sends a malicious call with a crafted amount that includes a path traversal attack.
findings.remediation: Use address[] to restrict sender and ensure only authorized addresses can call the function.

findings.title: Path Traversal in `getOwner` function
findings.explanation: This function allows an attacker to access files outside the intended directory by manipulating the `ownerIndex` parameter.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive files or configuration data
exploitation_steps: Manipulate the `ownerIndex` to point to a file outside the intended directory.
Call the `getOwner` function with the manipulated `ownerIndex`.
Retrieve or modify the contents of the accessed file.
findings.exploitation_conditions: The attacker has access to the current owner index.
findings.remediation: Use a validated and sanitized input to ensure the `ownerIndex` parameter is within the intended directory.
